We evaluate on MNIST (LeCun et al. , 1998 ) with a fully connected network of 4.36M parameters (architecture in Appendix G.1 ) and on CIFAR-10 (Krizhevsky, 2009 ) with a standard ResNet-18 (He et al. , 2016 ) . We consider two deletion settings: random 10% and classwise deletion, with additional results (including ViT-Tiny) in Appendix G . For NFT-based methods, we fix ( ε , δ ) (\varepsilon,\delta) per plot with δ = 10 − 5 \delta=10^{-5} and vary ε \varepsilon across plots. For each setting, we compute the minimal feasible noise scale σ \sigma (Theorem 1 ), derive the corresponding step budget T T , and run unlearning for T T steps (Block-wise NFT applies this sequentially across blocks), followed by standard fine-tuning. We cap the total number of unlearning+fine-tuning iterations at 1000 ( ≤ \leq 1.5 epochs at batch size 64 on 90% of the data). In practice, methods typically reach their peak accuracy well before the end of fine-tuning. Unless stated otherwise, we use Random Blocks (Section 4.3 ); other block designs are deferred to the appendix. Results are averaged over 5 runs to ensure statistical reliability. Figure 3 shows results for the random 10% deletion task.
